metadata.title: Adaptive MLP Pruning for Large Vision Transformers

concepts.statement: Large vision transformers scale well but their parameter, compute, and memory costs make deployment expensive.
MLP modules dominate parameter count (81.1% in the cited EVA-CLIP-E example), making them the highest-leverage structural pruning target.
One-hot cross entropy ignores non-label predictions during Taylor importance estimation and also prevents pruning models whose original heads or losses are unavailable.
Use the entropy of the full, label-free inter-instance similarity distribution both to score neurons and to stop block-wise binary-search pruning when prediction uncertainty changes too much.
Across the evaluated CLIP and DINOv2 models, AMP reduces MLP-heavy encoders substantially; knowledge distillation is essential for recovering near-original accuracy.

claims.statement: For the evaluated CLIP and DINOv2 backbones, AMP removes roughly 40% of encoder parameters and FLOPs, while the distilled models recover near-original performance on the reported tasks.
claims.scope: Four CLIP-style encoders on zero-shot classification/retrieval and five encoders including DINOv2-g on ImageNet-1K kNN; recovery is after ImageNet-1K distillation.

claims.statement: The four evaluated CLIP encoders run at roughly 1.5 times their original image throughput after pruning.
claims.scope: Single NVIDIA A6000 GPU, batch size 1000, 224x224 inputs; throughput averaged over 10 runs.

claims.statement: The label-free information-entropy criterion yields better pruning-only downstream accuracy than cross entropy at a comparable parameter count.
claims.scope: OpenCLIP-g, six zero-shot classification benchmarks, one criterion ablation.

claims.statement: Block-wise entropy-guided binary search performs much better than uniform Taylor pruning at a comparable OpenCLIP-g parameter count.
claims.scope: OpenCLIP-g pruning-only average accuracy over six zero-shot classification benchmarks.

claims.statement: The similarity-entropy formulation can prune a backbone without labels or access to its original prediction head, demonstrated on DINOv2-g.
claims.scope: Label-free ImageNet pruning/distillation and ImageNet-1K kNN evaluation of DINOv2-g.

methods.name: Label-free entropy Taylor scoring
methods.purpose: Rank MLP hidden neurons by how strongly removing them changes the model's full prediction-distribution uncertainty.

steps.description: Form pairwise cosine similarities from class-token image representations.
Apply a temperature-scaled row-wise softmax to obtain an inter-instance possibility distribution.
Compute mean information entropy over the mini-batch.
Use a first-order Taylor approximation of entropy sensitivity and aggregate each neuron across tokens.
Rank hidden neurons by absolute importance for structured removal.

assumptions: Inter-instance similarity is a useful prediction-distribution surrogate.
The first-order Taylor remainder is small enough for ranking.

methods.name: Block-wise adaptive MLP pruning
methods.purpose: Choose each MLP block's remaining hidden size without a single predefined global pruning ratio.

steps.description: Process transformer blocks from last to first and initialize the feasible hidden-size interval to [0, M0].
Prune to the interval midpoint and measure the resulting entropy.
If the entropy increase is below delta E, search a smaller hidden size; otherwise retain more neurons.
Stop after tmax steps or when the interval has size one, then carry the accepted model entropy to the next block.

assumptions: Entropy is approximately monotonic with retained hidden size over the searched interval.

methods.name: Token-level knowledge distillation
methods.purpose: Recover the pruned encoder's representation quality using the frozen original encoder as teacher.

steps.description: Run the same image through the frozen original encoder and the pruned student.
Match class-token and patch-token representations with normalized mean squared error.

assumptions: Pruning only MLP hidden dimensions preserves teacher/student output dimensions.

experiments.question: Can AMP reduce CLIP encoder size and compute while preserving zero-shot classification after distillation?
experiments.setup: Prune four CLIP encoders using 50,000 ImageNet-1K images, distill for 10 epochs on unlabeled ImageNet-1K, and evaluate six zero-shot classification datasets; throughput is measured on one A6000 GPU with batch size 1000.
limitations: Accuracy tables report no variance or statistical tests.
Throughput scope is one GPU, one batch size, and one resolution.
Pruning-only accuracy drops sharply for the two EVA models before distillation.

experiments.question: Does the compressed CLIP representation retain cross-modal retrieval quality?
experiments.setup: Evaluate text-to-image and image-to-text retrieval on Flickr30K and COCO using Recall@1/5/10 and mean recall.

results.value: 85.7→86.1 after distillation with parameters reduced from 7.53B to 4.59B

limitations: Only CLIP-style encoders are applicable to the cross-modal retrieval task.

experiments.question: Does AMP outperform alternative pruning strategies at comparable model size?
experiments.setup: Compare pruning-only and post-distillation average zero-shot classification accuracy for OpenCLIP-g and EVA-CLIP-E at matched parameter counts.

results.comparison: best competing post-distillation result; paper prose says 2.1%, inconsistent with the table

limitations: The stated 2.1% EVA-CLIP-E margin conflicts with the 1.4-point difference in Table 3.

experiments.question: Can the head-free criterion compress a pure vision transformer and recover representation quality?
experiments.setup: Evaluate last-block representations on ImageNet-1K with kNN for CLIP encoders and DINOv2-g.
limitations: One pure-vision backbone and one downstream protocol are reported.

experiments.question: Does information entropy improve the pruning ranking relative to cross entropy?
experiments.setup: Replace the information-entropy criterion with cross entropy and compare pruning-only OpenCLIP-g at roughly matched parameter counts.

results.value: 50.0% at 0.65B parameters versus 53.8% at 0.62B with information entropy

limitations: The experiment measures downstream accuracy, not importance-score fidelity directly.

experiments.question: Does adaptive block-wise sizing outperform uniform MLP sizing?
experiments.setup: Compare uniform Taylor pruning from hidden size 6144 to 2645 with AMP binary search at similar total parameter count.

results.comparison: uniform Taylor pruning versus AMP binary search

limitations: The paper prose reports 64.5%, which is not derivable from the table values.

understanding_path.transition: Most parameters sit in MLP modules.
A head-free uncertainty signal can replace one-hot loss.
The same signal drives scoring and adaptive stopping.
Separate pruning quality from recovery after distillation.
State only the scope supported by the tables.

analysis_warnings: Table 6 implies a 46.5 percentage-point gain (53.8-7.3), not the 64.5% stated in the prose.
Table 3 implies a 1.4 percentage-point EVA-CLIP-E distilled margin over NViT (81.0-79.6), not the 2.1% stated in the prose.
The Table 3 row label 'AMR (ours)' is treated as a typographical error for AMP.
Canonical LaTeX was manually transcribed from rendered equations because DocumentIR honestly records lossy pdf_text rather than source LaTeX.
